subject.title: Feature Request: Masked Secrets - Prevent Agent from Accessing Raw API Keys

question: Should OpenClaw make agent-executed credential isolation a supported core security boundary, and if so, which execution, provider, plugin, and output paths must be covered by the first design?
rationale: The requested guarantee changes the threat model and crosses credential storage, process execution, provider routing, plugin hooks, output persistence, and upgrade-sensitive operator behavior; source review cannot safely choose that contract without owner intent.

options.title: Sponsor a scoped core design
options.body: Define the supported threat model and an initial credential-injection/redaction boundary owned by the security and runtime surfaces.

options.title: Adopt a plugin-first contract
options.body: Document the existing hook surface as the supported extension route and specify any missing narrow SDK capability without promising core isolation.

options.title: Decline the guarantee
options.body: Document that host-level separation remains the required boundary for arbitrary agent command execution and close the request only with that explicit policy decision.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a scoped core design
recommendation.body: Define the supported threat model and an initial credential-injection/redaction boundary owned by the security and runtime surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The requested security boundary spans the secret-bearing paths routed to this owner boundary.
